title: Happy Children’s Day To Every Child
author: Uncle Emma

body.text: Celebrating Children's Day
Uncle Emma
5/27/2025 2 min read

body.alt: Happy Children’s Day To Every Child

body.text: Happy Children’s Day To Every Child
Today, the world pauses to celebrate its greatest treasure; our children.

As a father, I look at my son, Prince Eneojo Josiah, and I see more than a smile or a tiny hand reaching for mine. I see hope, I see tomorrow, I see the proof that God still entrusts this world with fresh chances to get it right.
Children’s Day is not just about balloons, songs, or colorful clothes. It is a reminder; a powerful one; that we are stewards of lives God holds dear.

At Catch Them Young Bible Club, we don’t just gather children to play or pass time. We gather them to build foundations; foundations of faith, character, purpose, and joy. We gather them because every child deserves to be seen, heard, and guided in the way of the Lord.
But let’s not forget; children are growing up in a world full of noise, pressure, and confusion.
They face:
Unfiltered content that pollutes innocence,
Peer pressure that pulls them into early compromise,
Homes that are loud with correction but silent in affection,
A society that often sees them as numbers, not souls.
But we believe differently.
We believe every child is a seed of greatness, waiting to be watered with truth, love, patience, and prayers.
We believe they are not just the leaders of tomorrow; they are the lights of today.
We believe that when Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me,” He meant it with urgency, with tenderness, and with eternal intention.
So today, I celebrate not just children, but childhood;
The laughter, the curiosity, the honesty, the trust, the wonder.
To every parent, guardian, and teacher:
Protect that wonder; feed that curiosity with the Word. Don’t be too busy to kneel and pray with them, or to tell them, “God loves you, and so do I.”
To every child under our care at CTYBC:
You matter. You are deeply loved. You are not too young to know God, to hear His voice, and to walk in His purpose.
Happy Children’s Day
Prince Sani Emmanuel Grace
Convener, Catch Them Young Bible Club (CTYBC)
A Father, A Builder, A Believer.

title: The Broken Calabash – A Lesson on Kindness for Every Young Child.
author: Uncle Emma

body.text: At Catch Them Young Bible Club (CTYBC), we believe that even small acts of kindness can change lives. Today, we visit Peace Village Lugbe, a village where a young girl learns that true greatness comes from helping others.
Uncle Emma
5/15/2025 2 min read

body.alt: The Broken Calabash – A Lesson on Kindness for Every Young Child.

body.text: The Story of Ada and the Beggar Woman
In Peace Village , where the harmattan wind blew red dust across the roads and market women sold fresh akara by the roadside, lived Ada , a 9-year-old girl with a heart as bright as her smile.
One afternoon, as Ada carried a calabash of garri home from the market, she saw an old woman sitting under a tree, her clothes torn, her hands trembling.
"Nne, are you hungry?" Ada asked.
The woman nodded weakly. "I have not eaten since yesterday."
Ada hesitated. The garri was for her family’s dinner. But then she remembered her Sunday School teacher’s words: "When you show kindness, you are serving God."
She knelt beside the woman, broke the garri into two, and gave her half.
"Thank you, my child," the woman whispered. "God will bless you."
That night, Ada’s mother noticed the half-empty calabash. "Ada, where is the rest?"
Ada lowered her head. "Mummy, I gave some to a hungry woman."
Instead of scolding her, her mother smiled. "Come, let me tell you a story."
The Tale of the King’s Disguise
Long ago, a great king wanted to test the hearts of his people. So he dressed as a poor beggar and walked through the village.
Most people ignored him. Some even chased him away.
But one little girl, Ngozi , saw him shivering in the cold. She gave him her only wrapper and a piece of roasted corn.
The next day, the king returned in his royal robes and announced:
"Because Ngozi showed kindness to a stranger, she will dine in my palace forever!"
The villagers were shocked. "If only we had known it was the king!"
But the king replied, "Whatever you do for the least of people, you do for me."
Ada’s Reward
Ada’s eyes sparkled. "Mummy, was that woman… an angel?"
Her mother laughed. "Maybe not an angel, but God sees every act of love. And one day, He will reward you—maybe here, maybe in heaven."
The next market day, Ada saw the old woman again—but this time, she was dressed well and holding a basket of fruits.
"My daughter," the woman said, "my son came back from the city and took me home. I prayed for you, and God told me to bless you." She handed Ada the basket.
📖 What the Bible Says:
- Proverbs 19:17 – Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord.
- Matthew 25:40 – Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for Me.
- Ephesians 4:32 – Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.
📝 CTYBC Takeaway Lessons for Our Nigerian Children & Teens:
✅ Kindness is never wasted —God sees every good deed.
✅ You don’t have to be rich to help —even small acts matter.
✅ True greatness is serving others , not just yourself.
✅ God often blesses us through people we least expect.
✅ Treat everyone with love, because they matter to God.
At CTYBC , we are raising a generation that knows kindness is true strength!
💬 Parents & Teachers: Let’s teach our children that a caring heart is more valuable than money.
"Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify God." – Matthew 5:16

title: The Treasure Box :  A Lesson on Honesty for Every Young Child
author: Uncle Emma

body.text: At Catch Them Young Bible Club (CTYBC), we believe in teaching God’s truth in ways that children, teens, and adolescents can understand. Today, we explore the value of honesty, not just as a rule, but as a mark of true strength. Let’s journey to a small town called Sabon Lugbe, where a young boy learns a lesson that changes his heart forever.
Uncle Emma
5/14/2025 2 min read

body.alt: The Treasure Box :  A Lesson on Honesty for Every Young Child

body.text: The Story of Tobi and the Missing Naira

In Sabon Lugbe , where the sound of grinding machines filled the air and children played football in the dusty streets, lived Tobi , a 10-year-old boy who loved helping his father in his small provisions store.

One evening, as Tobi arranged bottles of soft drinks on the shelf, he noticed something on the floor—a 500-naira note ! His heart pounded. That was enough to buy two meat pies and a Fanta —his favourite snack. He glanced around. No one was looking.
"If I take it, no one will know," he thought.
But as he folded the money in his palm, his stomach twisted. He remembered his father’s words: "Tobi, a good name is better than riches."
That night, Tobi couldn’t sleep. The money felt heavy in his pocket. The next morning, he went to his father with his head bowed.
"Papa… I found this money yesterday, and I kept it."
His father’s face was serious, but his eyes softened. "Come, let me tell you a story."
The Tale of the King’s Treasure Box
Long ago, in a faraway kingdom, a wise king gave his two sons identical treasure boxes .
"These boxes are special," he said. "One day, I will ask you to open them before me."
The first son, Prince Kola , was impatient. "What’s inside?" he wondered. One day, he pried it open and found gold coins! Excited, he spent them all on fine clothes and parties.
The second son, Prince Dayo , resisted curiosity. "Father said to wait," he reminded himself.
Years later, the king called his sons. "Bring your boxes."
Prince Kola’s box was empty . But when Prince Dayo opened his, the king smiled. "Because you obeyed, I now give you the keys to the royal treasury!
Tobi’s Lesson Learned
Tobi’s eyes widened. "So, Papa, honesty is like keeping the treasure box closed?"
"Yes," his father nodded. "Every time you choose honesty, God trusts you with greater things. That 500 naira was a test—and you passed!"
Tobi returned the money, and his father hugged him tightly.
📖 What the Bible Says:
- Proverbs 12:22 – The Lord detests lying lips, but He delights in those who tell the truth.
- Ephesians 4:25 – Put away falsehood and speak truthfully.
- Luke 16:10 – Whoever is faithful in small things will be trusted with much.
📝 CTYBC Takeaway Lessons for  Children & Teens:
✅ Honesty brings honor —even when no one is watching.
✅ A lie may hide today, but it will shame you tomorrow.
✅ God rewards integrity with greater blessings.
✅ True strength is doing what’s right, even when it’s hard.
✅ Your word is your bond—keep it pure.
At CTYBC , we are raising a generation that knows truth is not just a rule—it’s God’s way of life!
💬 Parents & Teachers: Let’s keep teaching our children that a good name shines brighter than gold.
"The Lord loves those who do right." – Psalm 11:7

title: Celebrating 11 Years of Catching Them Young
author: UNCLE EMMANUEL

body.text: Celebrating 11 Years of Catching Them Young
FROM UNCLE EMMA'S DESK
UNCLE EMMANUEL
5/3/2025 1 min read

body.alt: Celebrating 11 Years of Catching Them Young

body.text: Today, our hearts are full of gratitude as we celebrate 11 years of Catch Them Young Bible Club (CTYBC).

Eleven years ago, lying on a hospital bed after a life-threatening accident, I had an encounter that would forever change my life. It was in that moment of weakness that God entrusted me with a divine assignment—to raise His precious children, the future generals of His Kingdom.

From that moment to now, we have seen God's hand, His help, and His heart. Not a single outreach program has been cancelled in all these years. Through every challenge, every rainy day, every tight budget, and every season of doubt, God has shown up faithfully—again and again.

We’ve watched children grow not only in stature but in spirit, from curious little ones to confident believers. Today, our first set of children are undergraduates. And we know—we are witnessing the fruit of obedience, sacrifice, and above all, grace.
To every parent who trusted us, released their children, and stood with us—we see you, and we thank you. There is a CTYBC because of you. Your belief in this vision fuels us every day.
To our volunteers, supporters, and prayer warriors—you are part of every testimony.
And to the One who called us, carried us, and continues to lead us—Lord, we give You all the glory. Thank You for the honour of serving You through the lives of these little ones.
CTYBC is 11. The vision is alive. The fire still burns. And by His grace, the best is yet to come.
A story on listening to God amidst life’s noise
FROM UNCLE EMMA'S DESK
Emmanuel Sani
5/3/2025 2 min read
In the heart of Oluwada Village , where children played with old tires and chickens ran across sandy roads, lived a boy named Tomiwa . He was 13, loved football, music, and his new talking drum.
Tomiwa’s parents loved God and always prayed together. They often said, “God speaks, but only those with quiet hearts hear Him.”
Tomiwa wanted to hear God too. So he began waking up early to pray, carrying his Bible everywhere, and writing down memory verses.
But slowly… things began to change.
🎧 Noise Upon Noise
Tomiwa joined a new WhatsApp group. They shared jokes, played online games, and talked for hours. He also started following a popular influencer who said things like:
“God is old news. Just believe in yourself!”
At school, his friends talked about who was dating who , who was “crushing” , and which party to attend. Tomiwa laughed along. He didn’t want to feel left out.
Soon, his Bible stayed under his bed. His memory verses faded. His prayers became short. He didn’t even notice… his heart had become crowded.
The Dream That Changed Everything
One night, Tomiwa had a dream. He was in a garden, full of tall weeds, loud music, flashing lights, and people talking all at once.
In the middle was a small light. It flickered weakly and called his name softly. “Tomiwa… Tomiwa…”
But he couldn’t hear it well. The noise around him was too much.
He woke up sweating.
His Heart Begins to Clear
That morning, he knelt and cried. “God, is that how You’ve been calling me and I couldn’t hear?”
He remembered a verse his mummy once made him memorize:
“Be still, and know that I am God.” – Psalm 46:10
He also opened his Bible and saw:
“The worries of this life… choke the word, making it unfruitful.” – Matthew 13:22 (The Parable of the Sower)
“My sheep hear my voice; I know them, and they follow me.” – John 10:27
From that day, Tomiwa began removing the weeds from his heart.
He reduced screen time. He left groups that added noise, not value. He spent more quiet moments praying, journaling, and listening.
He reduced screen time.
He left groups that added noise, not value.
He spent more quiet moments praying, journaling, and listening.
And slowly… the light in his dream began to shine brighter in his real life.
💡 Lessons for Every Child and Teen

God is always speaking , but a noisy heart cannot hear Him. Distractions can be good things , like friends and fun—but if they crowd our hearts, we miss God’s voice. Make time for stillness. God whispers in quiet places. Clean your heart often. Like a garden, your heart needs weeding. Don’t be afraid to stand out. Even if others don’t understand, your relationship with God is worth it.

title: 🌸 The Garden of Secrets – A Lesson on Sexual Purity for Every Young Nigerian Child
author: Emmanuel Sani

body.text:
At Catch Them Young Bible Club (CTYBC), we are passionate about teaching God’s truth in a way that makes sense to children, adolescents and teens. One of the lessons close to our hearts is sexual purity—not just as a rule, but as a precious responsibility from God.

Let’s take a trip to a little Nigerian town called Bethel Village, where a young girl asked a question many of our children are quietly wondering about.
PARENTING
Emmanuel Sani
4/18/2025 2 min read

body.alt: 🌸 The Garden of Secrets – A Lesson on Sexual Purity for Every Young Nigerian Child

body.text: In Bethel Village, where goats bleat in the morning and mamas sell puff-puff on the roadside, lived Debby , a 12-year-old girl who loved helping her mummy water the flowers and boil yam for Sunday rice.
One sunny morning, as she helped her mother in the compound, she asked, “Mummy, why do some of my friends say they have boyfriends and do things they hide from adults?”
Her mum smiled and sat on the small wooden stool under the mango tree. “Come, Debby,” she said. “Let me tell you a story your grandma told me. A story about a prince and a garden.”
The Tale of Prince Zach’s Garden

In a nearby town, a young prince named Zach was given a beautiful garden by his father, the king. “This garden is precious,” the king said. “Guard it well. One day, I will send someone who deserves to walk in it with you.”
At first, Zach obeyed. He kept his garden clean and bright. But one day, his friends from the village said, “Ah-ah, Zach, allow people to visit now. Are you forming holy-holy?”
Zach gave in.
Soon, the garden was trampled. Some came and plucked the best flowers. Others left strange seeds. The beauty faded.
Zach wept and ran to his father. “Daddy, I messed up. I didn’t guard the garden.”
The king hugged him. “You’re still my son. I can help you start again. But this time, learn to say no and trust me.”
Zach did. And though it took time, the garden began to grow again—stronger and more beautiful than before.
Debby’s Eyes Opened
Debby looked up at her mum, her eyes wide.
“So, mummy, our bodies are like that garden?” “Exactly,” her mother smiled. “God gave you your body to keep pure, to protect, and to prepare for His purpose. Don’t let anyone trample on it.”
📖 What the Bible Says:

1 Corinthians 6:19-20 – Your body is God’s temple. Honor Him with it. Proverbs 4:23 – Guard your heart—it controls your life. 2 Timothy 2:22 – Run away from things that tempt you. Matthew 5:8 – Only the pure in heart will see God.

title: The Importance of Guiding Children Early: Insights from Proverbs 22:6

body.text: PARENTING
8/20/2024 2 min read
Understanding Proverbs 22:6: A Biblical Perspective

Proverbs 22:6 states, "Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it." This proverb emphasizes the significance of instilling values and teachings in children from a young age. The idea is that the lessons learned during childhood will stick with individuals throughout their lives, guiding their actions and decisions as they grow older.
Early Education and Character Building

The early years of a child's life are crucial for character development. When parents and educators focus on teaching children positive behaviors, moral values, and practical life skills, they lay a strong foundation for the child's future. These early lessons can help children develop empathy, resilience, and responsibility, qualities that will serve them well in various aspects of their lives.
The Advantages of Early Guidance
Guiding children from a young age offers several advantages:

1. Strong Moral Foundation: Teaching children the difference between right and wrong helps cultivate a moral compass, enabling them to make ethical decisions. 2. Lifelong Habits: Early training in good habits, such as discipline and respect, often leads to these behaviors becoming second nature. 3. Emotional Stability: Children who receive consistent guidance are better equipped to handle emotional challenges, leading to improved mental health. 4. Enhanced Learning: Early education can spark a love for learning, encouraging curiosity and intellectual growth.
Practical Ways to Teach Children
There are several practical methods parents and educators can use to teach and guide children:

Model Behaviors: Children often learn by observing the adults around them. Demonstrating positive behaviors can have a significant impact. Interactive Learning: Engaging children in hands-on activities and discussions makes learning more relatable and enjoyable. Consistent Reinforcement: Repeating lessons and maintaining consistent rules help reinforce what children have learned. Positive Reinforcement: Rewarding good behavior encourages children to continue acting positively.
Conclusion: Long-Lasting Impact

The teachings and values instilled in children from a young age, as suggested by Proverbs 22:6, can have a profound and lasting impact on their lives. Early guidance helps shape their character, moral values, and decision-making abilities, equipping them to face future challenges with confidence and integrity. Investing time and effort in teaching children early is a valuable endeavor that can yield benefits for a lifetime.

title: Protecting Purity, Guarding Innocence : A Message to the Next Generation
author: Emmanuel Sani

body.text: PARENTING
Emmanuel Sani
6/27/2025 3 min read

body.alt: Protecting Purity, Guarding Innocence : A Message to the Next Generation

body.text: This month, I began teaching my teenagers about something the world no longer speaks about enough, sexual purity . Not from a place of fear, but from understanding, wisdom, and strength.
We started with open conversations. Real conversations. I told them purity isn’t just about avoiding something, it’s about protecting something. It’s not about rules, it’s about value.

We used the story of Amnon and Tamar in 2 Samuel 13. How Amnon had evil intentions, and how his so-called friend Jonadab gave him a wicked plan, to deceive the king, pretend to be sick, and lure Tamar to his room. Tamar, thinking she was talking to someone who had sense, tried to reason with Amnon. She spoke the truth, warned him about the consequences, and begged him not to violate her. But he didn’t listen. He raped her.

I told my teenagers, in any compromising or odd situation, always believe that you might be the only wise person there. Act accordingly. Think fast. Leave if you have to. Never stay just because everyone else is quiet.

We talked about Jonadab, the kind of friend who gives you advice that sounds clever but will ruin your life. I told them, avoid friends like Jonadab . Because when trouble comes, those friends disappear and leave you holding the mess. Worse, they’ll tell the story of what you did and leave out what they caused.
We ended that session with this: choose godly friends, the ones who protect your vision, not stain it.

Then I shared another story, this time of Joseph. A young man who also found himself in a compromising situation. His master’s wife tried to seduce him. He reasoned with her, tried to speak sense. When he saw it wasn’t working, he ran. He left his coat behind, but he kept his integrity.

And here’s the powerful part: the Bible says, “Resist the devil and he will flee from you”, but when it comes to sexual temptation, we aren’t told to resist; we are told to flee . Run. Escape. Don’t try to negotiate sin. The Bible says, “Flee every appearance of evil.” If it starts to look like sin, run .
And then I mentioned something that still breaks me, how today, many children don’t just face danger from strangers, but from the very people they should be able to trust.

I showed them a skit by Gilmore: a boy and a girl talking late at night. The boy’s mother found them, punished them both, called the girl’s parents to inform them, and even requested that she be disciplined again when she got home. Many of us grew up in that kind of society, a world where any adult could correct you, and correction came from love, not shame.

But today, that safety net is broken. We have irresponsible uncles and aunties who are now a danger. Children are being molested in homes, schools, and churches. Not just girls; boys, too . And not just by strangers, but sometimes by family.
I told my teenagers, no matter who it is, if it feels wrong, say something . Report it to your parents. Don’t keep quiet. Protect yourself. Your body is not a playground. It is sacred.

And to every parent reading this, please, listen to your children . Don’t dismiss their discomfort. Don’t say, “you’re exaggerating.” If your child says someone made them uncomfortable, believe them first. Investigate, listen, support.

We must teach our children not just morality, but self-defence, emotional, spiritual, and physical. Teach them how to speak up. Teach them how to say “no.” Teach them that silence is not maturity when something is wrong.
If we’re going to raise a generation of light in a dark world, then we must do more than pray—we must prepare them, equip them, teach them.
Because purity is not weakness, it is strength under control.
And while the world may try to shame them into silence, we will teach them how to walk tall, with conviction, with courage, and with Christ.
